subject.title: Feature: Processing indicator message for Telegram (send ⌛️ while thinking, delete on reply)

question: Do Telegram status reactions sufficiently solve the perceived-silence problem, or should Telegram also send a standalone processing message that is deleted or edited?
rationale: The existing reaction lifecycle addresses the same user concern, but standalone messages have materially different visibility, chat noise, failure semantics, and configuration cost.

options.title: Add opt-in message
options.body: Keep status reactions and add a disabled-by-default Telegram placeholder for users who need stronger in-chat visibility.

options.title: Reactions are sufficient
options.body: Treat queued, thinking, done, and error reactions as the supported processing indicator and avoid another config surface.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in message
recommendation.body: Keep status reactions and add a disabled-by-default Telegram placeholder for users who need stronger in-chat visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: His current-main work owns the Telegram status-reaction behavior that must be compared with the requested placeholder UX.
